messages:
maya: FYI — Greenwave (acct gw-298) reported their API key never showed up in the console after onboarding via Okta SSO. Provisioner job shows completed. Customer tried a request and got 403 project_mismatch. I can repro locally with `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://api.redwood.com/v1/models` -> 403.
onboard-bot: Provisioner event: provisioner-342 completed for tenant gw-298 -> created service_key id sk_ABC123 bound_project internal-499 at 2026-03-15T12:03:20Z
eli: Hmm, that looks like the fallback path — keys sometimes land in the internal project when the org has no default project set. Can you paste the claim ID + full provisioner event and the project slug the customer expects?
maya: Claim: claim_873f. Provisioner snippet: 
```
INFO Provisioner finished for claim_873f -> svc_key: sk_ABC123
bound_project: internal-499
roles: [service_role]
```
Customer console shows org slug `greenwave` and project slug `gw-prod`. Customer says they never successfully called the API (all 403s).
jordan: I can rebind the key to gw-prod and update IAM bindings. Any need to rotate the key? If it was never used, safe to rebind. Also want an audit entry.
eli: Go ahead and rebind. Steps I usually run: 
1) `POST /admin/v1/keys/sk_ABC123/rebind` with body `{ "project": "gw-prod" }`
2) ensure `service_role` is present on `gw-prod` via `PUT /admin/v1/projects/gw-prod/policies`
I'll watch logs while you do it.
eli: (after) Done — admin log shows: `2026-03-15T12:09:02Z REBOUND sk_ABC123 -> gw-prod by eli`
maya: Customer retried and reports `curl` now returns 200 and model list. :tada: Leaving a note: root cause appears to be provisioner default-project fallback creating `internal-499` when org lacked a default project. Filed ENG-4521 to surface project selection in the onboarding flow and avoid internal-project sinks.
jordan: :thumbsup: I'll add a short postmortem blurb and link ENG-4521 to the provisioner backlog. Closing once customer confirms in 24h.
